ce:2023:q1.question:
For the integral

$\mathrm{I}=\int_{-1}^{1} \frac{1}{\mathrm{x}^{2}} \mathrm{dx}$

which of the following statements is TRUE?

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned}

I & =\int_{-1}^{1} \frac{1}{x^{2}} d x \\

& =2 \int_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{x^{2}} d x \quad(\because \quad f(-x)=f(x)) \\

& =2 \lim _{t \rightarrow 0^{+}} \int_{t}^{1} \frac{d x}{x^{2}} \\

& =2 \lim _{t \rightarrow 0^{+}}\left(\frac{-1}{x}\right)_{t}^{1} \\

& =-2 \lim _{t \rightarrow 0^{+}}\left(1-\frac{1}{t}\right) \\

& =2 \lim _{t \rightarrow 0^{+}}\left(\frac{1}{t}-1\right) \\

& =2 \lim _{h \rightarrow 0^{+}}\left(\frac{1}{0+h}-1\right)\\

& =2(\infty-1) \\

& =\infty \;\;\; (Divergent)

\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

ce:2023:q14.title: GATE CE 2023 | Set 1 | Question: 14
ce:2023:q14.question: If $M$ is an arbitrary real $n \times n$ matrix, then which of the following matrices will have non-negative eigenvalues?

detailed_solution.markdown:
$M X=\lambda X$

$[\lambda$ is eigen value of $(M)]$

$$\begin{aligned}

M M X & =\lambda M X \\

M^{2} X & =\lambda(\lambda X) \\

M^{2} X & =\lambda^{2} X

\end{aligned}$$

$\left[\lambda^{2}\right.$ (non negative) is eigen value of $\left.\mathrm{M}^{2}\right]$

$$\begin{aligned}

M X & =\lambda X \\

M^{\top} X & =\lambda X

\end{aligned}$$

$\left[M, M^{\top}\right.$ have same eigen values]

$$\begin{aligned}

& M M^{\top} X=\lambda M X \\

& M M^{\top} X=\lambda(\lambda X) \\

& M M^{\top} X=\lambda^{2} X

\end{aligned}$$

$\left[\lambda^{2}\right.$ (none negative) is eigen value of $\left.M M^{\top}\right]$

$$\begin{aligned}

M X & =\lambda X \\

M^{\top} X & =\lambda X \\

M^{\top} M X & =\lambda M X \\

M^{\top} M X & =\lambda(\lambda X) \\

M^{\top} M X & =\lambda^{2} X

\end{aligned}$$

$\left[\lambda^{2}\right.$ (non negative) is eigen value of $\left.M^{\top} M\right]$

$$\begin{aligned}

M X & =\lambda X \\

M M X & =\lambda M X \\

M^{2} X & =\lambda(\lambda X)

(M^T)^2 X&= \lambda ^2 X

\end{aligned}$$

$\left[\because M, M^{\top}\right.$ have same eigen value]

$\left(M^{\top}\right)^{2} X=\lambda^{2} X$

[ $\lambda^{2}$ is eigen value of $\left(M^{\top}\right)^{2}$ which non negative] Hence, option A, B, C, D are correct.

Therefore, the correct option(s) are **A, B, C, D**.

So, $b_{n}$ depends on $p$.

ce:2023:q19.question: The probabilities of occurrences of two independent events $A$ and $B$ are $0.5$ and $0.8$, respectively. What is the probability of occurrence of at least $A$ or $B$ (rounded off to one decimal place)?

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned}

& P(A)=0.5 \\

& P(B)=0.8

\end{aligned}$$

Probability of occurence of atleast $A$ or $B=$ $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A} \cap \mathrm{B})$

$$\begin{aligned}

P(A \cap B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A \cap B) \\

& =0.5+0.8-P(A) \times P(B) \\

& =0.5+0.8-0.5 \times 0.8 \\

& =1.3-0.4 \\

& =0.9

\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **0.9**.

Radius of circular curve $(\mathrm{R})=300 \mathrm{~m}$

$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{d}}=15 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$

ce:2023:q27.title: GATE CE 2023 | Set 1 | Question: 27
ce:2023:q27.question: Consider a doubly reinforced RCC beam with the option of using either Fe250 plain bars or Fe500 deformed bars in the compression zone. The modulus of elasticity of steel is $2 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{mm}^{2}$. As per IS456-2000, in which type(s) of the bars, the stress in the compression steel $\left(f_{s c}\right)$ can reach the design strength $\left(0.87 f_{y}\right)$ at the limit state of collapse?
options:
Both Fe250 plain bars and Fe500 deformed
bars

Neither Fe250 plain bars nor Fe500 deformed
bars

detailed_solution.markdown:
In a doubly reinforced beam, at the limit state of collapse. The strain in the extreme corression fibre will be $0.0035$. As the compression reinforcement will be below this, the strain in if will be always less than $0.0035$.

For Fe250, the yield strain

$=\frac{0.87 \times 250}{2 \times 10^{5}}=0.0010875$

For Fe500, the yield strain

$$\begin{aligned}

& =0.002+\frac{0.87 \mathrm{f}_{y}}{E_{s}} \\

& =0.002+\frac{0.87 \times 500}{2 \times 10^{5}} \\

& =0.004175>0.0035

\end{aligned}$$

So, it is possible that $\mathrm{Fe} 250$ can reach upto its yield strain and hence can reach the design strength $0.87 \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{y}}$.

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2023:q31.question:
Consider that a force $P$ is acting on the surface of a half-space (Boussingesq's problem). The expression for the vertical stress $\left(\sigma_{z}\right)$ at any point $(r, z)$ with the half-space is given as,

$\sigma_{z}=\frac{3 P}{2 \pi} \frac{z^{3}}{\left(r^{2}+z^{2}\right)^{5 / 2}}$

where, $r$ is the radial distance, and $z$ is the depth with downward direction taken as positive. At any given $r$, there is a variation of $\sigma_{z}$ along $z$, and at a specific $z$, the value of $\sigma_{z}$ will be maximum. What is the locus of the maximum $\sigma_{z}$ ?

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Stress Distribution in the Soil
detailed_solution.markdown:
The expression for the vertical stress $\left(\sigma_{2}\right)$ at any point $(r, z)$ with the half-space is given as

$\sigma_{z}=\frac{3 P}{2 \pi} \frac{z^{3}}{\left(r^{2}+z^{2}\right)^{5 / 2}}$

For $\sigma_{\mathrm{z}}$ to be maximum

$$\begin{aligned}

& \frac{\sigma_{z}}{\partial z}=0 \Rightarrow \frac{3 P}{2 \pi} \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left[\frac{z^{3}}{\left(r^{2}+z^{2}\right)^{5 / 2}}\right] \\

&=\frac{3 P}{2 \pi} \frac{\left[\left(r^{2}+z^{2}\right)^{5 / 2}-z^{3} \times \frac{5}{2}\left(r^{2}+z^{2}\right)^{3 / 2} \times 2 z\right]}{\left(r^{2}+z^{2}\right)^{5}}=0 \\

&=\left[\left(r^{2}+z^{2}\right)\left(3 z^{2}\right)-5 z^{4}\right]=0 \\

&=3 r^{2}+3 z^{2}=5 z^{2} \\

& z^{2}=\frac{3 r^{2}}{2}

\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

ce:2023:q35.title: GATE CE 2023 | Set 1 | Question: 35
ce:2023:q35.question:
In the following table, identify the correct set of associations between the entries in Column-1 and Column-2.
$$\begin{array}{|l|l|} \hline \text{Column-1} & \text{Column-2} \\ \hline \text{P : Reverse Osmosis} & \text{I: Ponding} \\ \hline \text{Q: Trickling Filter} & \text{II : Freundlich Isothrem} \\ \hline \text{R : Coagulation} &\text{ III : Concentration Polarization} \\ \hline \text{S : Adsorption} & \text{IV : Charge Neutralization} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Analysis of Unit Operations and Phenomena:**
  - **P. Reverse Osmosis $\rightarrow$ III. Concentration Polarization:**
    - In pressure-driven membrane separation (reverse osmosis), the semipermeable membrane rejects solute while permitting solvent water to permeate.
    - This produces a steep concentration gradient of retained solutes in a thin boundary layer immediately adjacent to the membrane feed surface. This phenomenon is termed **concentration polarization**, which increases local osmotic pressure and reduces permeate flux. $\implies \mathbf{P - III}$.
  - **Q. Trickling Filter $\rightarrow$ I. Ponding:**
    - In attached-growth trickling filters, excessive accumulation of microbial biofilm (excess biomass) clogs the void spaces between the filter media packing.
    - Wastewater cannot percolate downward freely and accumulates as stagnant pools on top of the filter bed, an operational defect known as **ponding**. $\implies \mathbf{Q - I}$.
  - **R. Coagulation $\rightarrow$ IV. Charge Neutralization:**
    - Naturally occurring colloidal impurities carry negative surface charges, creating mutually repulsive electrostatic forces that prevent agglomeration.
    - Addition of hydrolyzing metal coagulants (such as alum or ferric chloride) releases multivalent cations that compress the electrical double layer and neutralize negative colloid surface charges, allowing micro-flocs to coalesce. $\implies \mathbf{R - IV}$.
  - **S. Adsorption $\rightarrow$ II. Freundlich Isotherm:**
    - The equilibrium uptake of dissolved organic solutes onto solid adsorbents (such as granular activated carbon) is mathematically modeled by adsorption isotherms, most commonly the empirical **Freundlich isotherm**:
      $$\frac{x}{m} = k C_e^{1/n}$$
      $\implies \mathbf{S - II}$.

- **Synthesis:**
  - The complete matching is $P \rightarrow \text{III}, \; Q \rightarrow \text{I}, \; R \rightarrow \text{IV}, \; S \rightarrow \text{II}$.
  - Option D correctly contains the verified association subset: **P-III, Q-I, R-IV**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option D (P-III, Q-I, R-IV)**.

& v_{f}=\text { Free flow speed }=u_{B} \\

ce:2023:q42.title: GATE CE 2023 | Set 1 | Question: 42
ce:2023:q42.question:
The differential equation,

$\frac{\mathrm{du}}{\mathrm{dt}}+2 \mathrm{tu}^{2}=1$

is solved by employing a backward differnce scheme within the finite difference framework. The value of $u$ at the $(n-1)^{\text {th }}$ time-step, for some $n$, is 1.75. The corresponding time $(\mathrm{t})$ is $3.14 \mathrm{~s}$. Each time step is $0.01 \mathrm{~s}$ long. Then, the value of $(u_{n}-u_{n-1})$ is ____ (round off to three decimal places).

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned}

\frac{d u}{d t} & =1-2 t u^{2} \\

\frac{d u}{d t} & =f(t, u) \\

\Rightarrow \quad f(t, u) & =1-2 \mathrm{tu}^{2}

\end{aligned}$$

Eulers backward difference scheme

$$\begin{aligned}

u_{n}-u_{n-1} & =h f\left(t_{n}, u_{n}\right)=h\left(1-2 t_{n} u n^{2}\right) \\

& =0.01\left(1-2 \times 3.14 \times 1.75^{2}\right) \\

& =-0.1822

\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **-0.1505** (acceptable range: [-0.152, -0.149]).

ce:2023:ga:q1.title: GATE CE 2023 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 1
ce:2023:ga:q1.question:
"I have not yet decided what I will do this evening;
I _____ visit a friend."

detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Given Sentence:**
  - *""I have not yet decided what I will do this evening; I _____ visit a friend.""*
  - Options: (A) mite, (B) would, (C) might, (D) didn't.

- **Governing Principles:**
  - Modal auxiliary verbs indicate probability, certainty, intention, or possibility.
  - The preceding clause *"I have not yet decided what I will do this evening"* explicitly establishes that the speaker's future schedule is unresolved, tentative, and undecided.

- **Analytical Derivation:**
  - In standard English grammar:
    - **"Might"** is the modal auxiliary expressing tentative possibility or hypothetical intention about future events (i.e., "it is possible that I will visit a friend").
    - It aligns with the speaker's undecided state of mind.
    - Thus, the completed sentence reads: *"I have not yet decided what I will do this evening; I might visit a friend."*

- **Distractor Analysis:**
  - Option A (*"mite"*) is a noun denoting a minute arachnid or a small sum of money; it is a phonetic homophone and grammatically incorrect.
  - Option B (*"would"*) expresses habitual past actions, definite conditional consequences, or firm intention, which conflicts with *"have not yet decided"*.
  - Option D (*"didn't"*) is the past-tense negative auxiliary (*did not*), which creates a tense mismatch with the future time marker *"this evening"*.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option C (might)**.

- **Given Analogy:**
  - $\text{Eject} : \text{Insert} :: \text{Advance} : \underline{\hspace{1cm}}$
  - Options: (A) Advent, (B) Progress, (C) Retreat, (D) Loan.

- **Governing Principles:**
  - In a verbal analogy of the form $A : B :: C : D$, the relation connecting term $A$ to term $B$ must hold identically between term $C$ and term $D$.

- **Analytical Derivation:**
  - **Relationship between $A$ and $B$ ($\text{Eject} : \text{Insert}$):**
    - *"Eject"* means to throw out, expel, or remove from within.
    - *"Insert"* means to place, push, or put something into something else.
    - Thus, "Eject" and "Insert" are direct **antonyms** (exact opposites in meaning and physical direction).
  - **Applying the Relationship to $C$ ($\text{Advance}$):**
    - *"Advance"* means to move forward purposefully, make progress, or proceed toward an objective.
    - The direct antonym of advancing or moving forward is moving backward, withdrawing, or pulling back, which is **"Retreat"**.
    - Therefore, the required term is **Retreat**.

- **Distractor Analysis:**
  - Option A (*"Advent"*) means the arrival or appearance of a notable event or person, not opposite to advance.
  - Option B (*"Progress"*) is a synonym of advance, representing the exact reverse of the required antonym relationship.
  - Option D (*"Loan"*) refers to borrowing or lending financial assets, semantically unrelated to motion.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option C (Retreat)**.

$\log _{b} a \lt 1$ and $\log _{a} b \gt 1$

A square of side length $4 \mathrm{~cm}$ is given. The boundary of the shaded region is defined by one semi-circle on the top and two circular arcs at the bottom, each of radius $2 \mathrm{~cm}$, as shown.
The area of the shaded region is $\mathrm{cm}^{2}$.

Top shaded area $=4 \times 2-\frac{\pi 2^{2}}{2}=8-2 \pi$

Bottom shaded area $=\frac{\pi \times 2^{2}}{4} \times 2=2 \pi$

Total shaded area $=8-2 \pi+2 \pi=8$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.
